verdictHistory.supersededReason: RECLASSIFIED REJECTED/FAILED (CC-11.9, Product Owner correction + independent re-audit against the actual pixels, not re-asserted on authority alone). The original PASS incorrectly treated the absence of N/S pole identity as an acceptable deferral to a deterministic overlay. On CC-11.9 re-inspection: (1) no N or S label/marking of any kind is present anywhere in the image -- confirmed by direct re-inspection; (2) the field-line arrows are NOT self-consistent -- the two horizontal rays at the magnet's ends and the nested arc loops imply OPPOSITE pole assignments. Tracing the horizontal rays: the left ray's arrowhead points further left (away from the magnet -- outward flow at the left end); the right ray's arrowhead points left, i.e. toward/into the magnet (inward flow at the right end). That pattern alone implies LEFT=N (field exits), RIGHT=S (field enters). Tracing the arc loops instead: every loop's peak arrowhead (top set and bottom set) points left, meaning flow along each loop runs right-to-left -- consistent with exiting the RIGHT end and entering the LEFT end, i.e. RIGHT=N, LEFT=S. These two readings directly contradict each other on which end is N and which is S. A field-line diagram whose own arrows disagree with each other about pole identity is a genuine technical defect, not a matter of deferred labelling. This is independently confirmed on this re-inspection (not merely restated from the correction brief), though the precise original description ('arrows added to partial/incomplete field lines') does not exactly match this image -- every visible line here reads as a complete, closed loop or a full-length ray, not a truncated one; the defect is a direction self-contradiction between complete lines, which is the substantively same class of error (an unearned directional claim) even if the mechanism differs slightly from the original description.

factChecks.note: Concentric-loop dipole field pattern with the same tiered arc structure (multiple nested loops above and below the bar plus one straight central line each side) as the DipolMagnet.svg reference. Topology matches: loops emerge from one pole, curve around, and terminate at the other, symmetric above/below the bar. This part of the original finding still holds.

factChecks.fact: external field direction runs N to S
factChecks.note: N and S are not identified anywhere in the image (no label, no colour-coding, no marking of any kind), and the visible arrowheads contradict each other on which end the field exits vs enters (see verdictHistory for the specific contradiction between the horizontal-ray arrows and the arc-loop arrows). A learner cannot determine -- and the image does not correctly assert -- which end is N and which is S. This is a hard requirement for this asset per the CC-11.9 correction: required pole identity and direction semantics must be present and correct in the final image itself, not deferred to a later overlay.

factChecks.note: Not applicable to this state (density_comparison=false) -- no density-comparison claim is made by this image.

prohibitedChangeChecks.prohibition: do not draw field lines that reverse direction or cross incorrectly
prohibitedChangeChecks.note: Re-audited: the loop-arrow direction contradicts the horizontal-ray-arrow direction on pole assignment (see verdictHistory). This is exactly the class of error this prohibition exists to catch -- field-line arrows that cannot all be simultaneously correct for one consistent magnet -- and was missed on the original attempt-1 pass, which checked only whether individual loops were internally self-consistent, not whether all lines agreed with each other.

The magnet bar's material rendering remains a strong match to the premium/industrial-precision character.
physicalImplausibilityNotes: None beyond the arrow self-contradiction and missing pole identity noted above.
overallFindings: REJECTED on CC-11.9 re-audit. Two disqualifying defects, both confirmed by direct re-inspection of the actual pixels: (1) no N/S pole identity anywhere in the image; (2) the field-line arrows are directionally self-contradictory (horizontal rays and arc loops imply opposite pole assignments). The original PASS is invalid and is superseded -- see verdictHistory. This master is retained on disk as failed evidence only; it is not approved art and must not be treated as production-ready. A corrected regeneration is required, sending real reference bytes plus explicit N/S + direction requirements per the corrected asset contract, against the new white/near-white style guide.
